QUESTION
is it permitted to isntall circuit from one title into another
ANSWER
Practitioner summary
Outcome: Based only on the cited clauses - apply the requirements below to the installation and use any verification items as applicable.
Installing a circuit from one title into another is conditionally permitted. Effective segregation must be ensured when conductors for different
electrical installations are installed in a common enclosure. However, this requirement does not apply to switchboards where such circuits originate
or terminate.
What the cited clauses require
- Conductors for different electrical installations must be effectively segregated within a common enclosure.
- Effective segregation can be achieved by independently sheathed cables, barriers of fire-resisting material, or by maintaining a minimum
distance of 50 mm.
Exceptions, notes, and edge cases
- The segregation requirement does not apply to switchboards at which such circuits originate or terminate.

Required actions or sequencing
- Ensure effective segregation of conductors in common enclosures unless at a switchboard.
Confirm on site or in design records
- Whether the installation involves a switchboard where circuits originate or terminate.
Citations
- 3.9.8.2.2 - Effective segregation requirement and exception for switchboards.

QUESTION
what is the rule that control whether a circuit form one zone can be installed in a second zone
ANSWER
Practitioner summary
Outcome: Based only on the cited clauses - apply the requirements below to the installation and use any verification items as applicable.
The installation of a circuit from one zone into a second zone depends on ensuring protection against harmful influences and segregation
requirements. Circuits must be protected against injury or property damage due to harmful influences between different installations or circuits.
Segregation is required to prevent detrimental effects between circuits of different voltage levels.
What the cited clauses require
- Protection shall be provided against injury or property damage due to harmful influences between different electrical installations or circuits
(1.5.11.5).
- Circuits operating at different voltages must be protected against harmful effects of faults, which may be achieved by segregation or
overvoltage protection (1.5.11.2).
- Wiring systems must avoid detrimental effects between different parts of the same installation or circuits operating at different voltages
(3.9.8.1).

- Cables of high voltage circuits and low or extra-low voltage circuits shall not be enclosed in the same wiring system unless specific conditions
are met (3.9.8.3).
Exceptions, notes, and edge cases
- SELV and PELV circuit conductors may be contained within the same wiring system as low voltage circuits if installed in accordance with Clause
3.9.8.3 (7.5.4).
- Segregation requirements do not apply to switchboards at which circuits originate or terminate (3.9.8.2.2).
Required actions or sequencing
- Ensure adequate segregation or insulation between circuits of different voltage levels.
- Verify compliance with specific conditions for enclosing cables of different voltage levels in the same wiring system.
Confirm on site or in design records
- Specific voltage levels of the circuits involved.
- Whether the installation involves SELV or PELV circuits.
Citations

- 1.5.11.2 - Protection against harmful effects of faults between circuits of different voltages.

QUESTION
what is requirement of emergency light in class 6 building
ANSWER
Practitioner summary
Outcome: Based only on the cited clauses - apply the requirements below to the installation and use any verification items as applicable.
Emergency lighting is required in a Class 6 building in specific areas such as fire-isolated stairways, passageways, and rooms with certain floor areas.
The requirements depend on the layout and size of the building, particularly if the storey or room exceeds certain area thresholds.
What the cited clauses require
- Install emergency lighting in every fire-isolated stairway, passageway, or ramp.
- Install emergency lighting in every storey of a Class 6 building where the storey has an area more than 300 m².
- Install emergency lighting in rooms with a floor area more than 100 m² that do not open to a corridor or space with emergency lighting or to a
road or open space.
- Install emergency lighting in rooms with a floor area more than 300 m².
- Install emergency lighting in every room or space with public access in a Class 6 building if the storey area is more than 300 m² or if any point
on the floor is more than 20 m from the nearest doorway leading directly to a stairway, ramp, passageway, road, or open space.

Exceptions, notes, and edge cases
- Emergency lighting is not required in a farm building where automatic back-up power is provided by a fuel-driven generator or where no
artificial lighting is provided.
- In a bulk grain storage facility, the spacing of emergency lights can be increased to twice the distance required for Class 7 buildings.
Required actions or sequencing
- Verify the floor area of each storey and room in the Class 6 building.
- Check the layout to determine the path of travel to exits and the distance to doorways.
- Ensure compliance with AS/NZS 2293.1 for emergency lighting systems.
Confirm on site or in design records
- Exact floor area of each storey and room in the building.
- Presence of corridors or spaces with existing emergency lighting.
- Distance from any point on the floor to the nearest exit.
Citations
- E4D2 - Emergency lighting is required in specific areas of a Class 6 building.
- SA E4D2 - Exceptions for farm buildings and bulk grain storage facilities.

QUESTION
what is the rule about overloading the supply capacity device for short periods
ANSWER
Practitioner summary
Outcome: On the basis of the cited clauses alone, the described arrangement appears permitted (subject to the usual on-site checks).
Overloading the supply capacity device is permitted for short periods under specific conditions. Electrical installations must not exceed 130% of the
Distributor's nominated supply capacity for more than 2 hours. This can be managed using circuit breakers with specific thermal trip unit settings.
What the cited clauses require
- Electrical installations shall not exceed 130% of the Distributor's nominated supply capacity for more than 2 hours.
- Circuit breakers must comply with IEC/AS 60947 or IEC/AS 60898 standards.
- Circuit breakers must have a fixed thermal trip unit setting of 130% or 145% of the rated current, depending on the standard.
Required actions or sequencing
- Use circuit breakers complying with IEC/AS 60947 with a fixed thermal trip unit setting of 130% of the rated current.

- Use circuit breakers complying with IEC/AS 60898 with a fixed thermal trip unit setting of 145% of the rated current, de-rated to achieve 130%
of the nominated supply capacity.
- Adjustable circuit breakers are acceptable if the thermal trip unit is set to the nominated supply capacity and the overload duration is agreed
with the Distributor.
Citations
- 6.7.1.2 - Electrical installations shall not exceed 130% of the Distributor's nominated supply capacity for more than 2 hours.

what are the rules associated iwth mixed circuits

protected against harmful effects of faults, which can be achieved through segregation or overvoltage protection. SELV and PELV circuits have

- SELV and PELV circuits must be electrically separated from each other and from higher voltage circuits, except as allowed by specific clauses
(7.5.4).

- SELV and PELV circuit conductors may be contained within the same wiring system as low voltage circuits if installed in accordance with Clause
3.9.8.3 (7.5.4).

- Ensure effective segregation of circuits operating at different voltage levels (3.9.8.3).
- Provide overvoltage protection where necessary (2.7.1).

- Specific installation details to determine applicable exceptions or additional requirements.
